value="<ul><li>Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN)</li><li>Specificity = TN / (TN + FP)</li><li>Precision = TP / (TP + FP)</li><li>Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)</li><li>F₁-score = harmonic mean of precision and sensitivity</li><li>MCC = (TP·TN − FP·FN) / √[ (TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN) ]</li><li>Cohen’s κ = (pₒ − pₑ) / (1 − pₑ)</li></ul>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="270" width="460" value="The two error cells do not cost the same. A false positive leads to a confirmatory test;<br>a false negative delays treatment, which is why sensitivity is reported alongside accuracy." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="1040" x="150" y="390" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ylcKGnaQItZqe5hiTNBQ-2" parent="1" style="whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;glass=0;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#78909C;strokeWidth=2;fontColor=#37474F;fontFamily=Arial;fontSize=14;fontStyle=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;rounded=1;arcSize=6;" value="Metrics derived from the matrix" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="46" width="230" x="840" y="30" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
The two error cells do not cost the same. A false positive leads to a confirmatory test;
a false negative delays treatment, which is why sensitivity is reported alongside accuracy.
